faq.a: Rehani is associated with the Arabic form رَيْحَان, whose core sense is rehani; fragrant plant, basil (swahili form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Rehani?
faq.a: Rehani is associated with Arabic. Rehani is the Swahili form of Arabic رَيْحَان (Rayḥān), meaning 'fragrant plant, basil'; it occurs in the Quran.
Yes — the underlying form رَيْحَان is Arabic.
Rehani can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Rehani should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Rayḥān occurs in the Quran as a term for fragrant plants.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
